bloks.name: STRAIGHT UP
bloks.title: Find Your Edge
bloks.dek: The line between discipline and the untamed energy that belongs only to you.

body.text: Find your edge is the line between discipline and untamed energy that belongs only to you.

body.cap: What finding your edge looks like.

body.text: Many of us inherit expectations and habits that were never meant to be ours.
Finding your edge means stripping that away, putting your needs first — not as selfishness, but as oxygen.
And once you make that decision, you start to move with purpose.

bloks.name: WORD MEME
bloks.title: A Major Loser Known as Mr. Too Late
bloks.dek: How an insult became a signal.

body.text: If we were—low-key—doing a “best of 2025,” it’d be hard to ignore Donald Trump’s two-part public shot at Jerome Powell — branding him a Major Loser and tagging him as Mr. Too Late.
…Major Loser stopped being an insult and became a signal…
For those who view the Federal Reserve as an opaque power center that prints digital money, it felt like a small win — a dart thrown at Goliath that landed.
For others who can’t stand Trump, it was simply more evidence of his abrasive, and to many, classless style.

body.cap: A meme that knows its origin.
body.alt: Uncle Sam-style poster of Jerome Powell: I want you to be a major loser.

body.text: Soon after it landed in April 2025, Major Loser stopped being an insult and became a signal — repeatable, shareable, and t-shirt ready 😉
It was a single, cartoonish phrase that let Joe Public step into the moment and be instantly understood.
Language is power. Memes are how it moves.

body.alt: White T-shirt with Jerome Powell’s face and the words Mr Too Late.

body.cap: The ad for Toma AI. Watch on YouTube.

body.text: The ad borrows the language and rhythm of car sales to promote AI software for dealerships.
The task wasn’t explaining the product, it was making something operational feel watchable.
Originally built as a marketing video for Toma AI, it became the foundation for what’s now Unruly Reels, an AI-native advertising studio.
Takeaway: If you’re working with familiar tropes, do it with depth and intent.

bloks.name: CHAIN REACTION
bloks.title: What Is Kaspa? — The Playground Edition
bloks.dek: A simple way to understand how Kaspa moves digital money faster.

body.text: Kaspa is like a super-fast playground for digital money — much quicker than older systems like Bitcoin.
Most playgrounds have one slide (like how Bitcoin processes transactions one by one). Kids have to wait in a single line, which can take a while.
Kaspa’s playground is built differently. Instead of one slide, it has many slides, letting more things happen at once.
This means:

items: No waiting: Many kids (transactions) can go down different slides at the same time.
Super speed: You don’t have to wait long to know if your money made it to where it needed to go — it’s almost instant.

body.text: So Kaspa is like a playground where nobody’s stuck waiting in line, in the safest neighborhood of the city.

body.cap: Kaspa, explained. Made with Napkin AI (see TOOLZ).
body.alt: Chat-style explainer: Kaspa is a super-fast playground for digital money.

body.text: In 2025, Clipse made their presence felt with “So Be It.”
Heading into 2026, it would’ve been wrong not to tip the hat to the Virginia Beach brothers — Gene “Malice” and Terrence “Pusha T” Thornton.

Clipse carried a feel-good kind of charm in 2025 that’s likely to turn into nostalgia sooner than we expect — like finding something we didn’t realize we lost, then wanting to sit with it and savor the moment.
On the production
Pharrell was the seasoning they may have needed, in full control of the production on the hit single, which was released as a music video exclusively on Instagram on June 17, 2025.
Visually
As for the release itself: the visuals felt intentional with the right amount of space to breathe — a braggadocious juxtaposition with elegance.

The “culturally inappropriate” vocal sample, the Saudi Arabian audio theme, and a video that ultimately feels like a mish-mash of great 20th-century cinematic directors — Hitchcock, Kubrick, even flashes of Tarantino’s Sin City — in a way that works.
Stepping back
To some (including me), it’s not perfect — but what is? And honestly, it feels perfect for them, and that’s what matters.
Worth noting

Earlier this year, I went down the Clipse rabbit hole — interviews, backstory, how it all came together. The story of Clipse themselves — and this song — deserves far more space than this format allows.
So be it.

body.text: It feels like everything from the ’90s is being rediscovered and crowned iconic — college basketball included.
The 1992 Grant Hill inbounds to Christian Laettner — catch, shoot, score — is hands down one of the greatest sports moments in history.

body.alt: Christian Laettner celebrates after The Shot, 1992

body.text: Back when hype didn’t feel manufactured — when moments just happened.
Was this the beginning of sports media hype — or the peak? Maybe both.
Down one. Seconds left… ▶️

bloks.name: NOW PLAYING
bloks.title: Big Trouble in Little China
bloks.dek: The Pork Chop Express rolls out — and the tone is set.

body.text: Big Trouble in Little China (1986) is John Carpenter’s cult-action film starring Kurt Russell as trucker Jack Burton.
What makes it sing is Russell’s Jack: cocky, clueless, all-American bravado played like comedy genius.
That opening radio-dispatch monologue over the ’80s groove, rolling the big rig, is peak Burton—enjoy.
